text:
Samir: heads up — running a terraform plan for the tenant-namespaces module and it wants to add an IAM role binding for a SA that already exists in the cluster. not sure if the helm chart or TF should win here.

Morgan: can you paste the diff? likely the helm values dropped the `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn` annotation and TF is trying to re-add it.

Samir: yeah. plan shows this:```hcl
resource "aws_iam_role" "tenant_ns_role" {
  name = "redwood-tenant-{{namespace}}-sa"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.irsa.json
}
resource "kubernetes_service_account" "uploader_sa" {
  metadata {
    name = "uploader"
    namespace = var.namespace
    annotations = {
      "eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn" = aws_iam_role.tenant_ns_role.arn
    }
  }
}
```

Samir: but the helm release for the uploader chart is setting SA via `values.serviceAccount.create = false` and `values.serviceAccount.name = uploader` — so chart manages the SA metadata. helm values currently have no annotations.

Tess: ok that means we have two control planes colliding: helm (cluster) vs terraform (iam + sa). We need a reconciliation playbook to avoid drift and avoid helm deleting the annotation on upgrades.

Alex: options: 1) let TF manage the SA completely (set helm to not touch SA, `serviceAccount.create = false` and ensure helm not patching metadata), 2) let helm own SA and have TF only create the IAM role and use `kubernetes_manifest` to patch the SA with annotation (risky), 3) use a null_resource with `kubectl annotate` in TF after apply.

Morgan: prefer option 1 for predictable infra ownership. For tenant namespaces we already have a pattern: TF creates the namespace + role + SA annotation, and charts consume the SA name with `create=false`. We should standardize and add a lint check.

Samir: sounds good. one wrinkle: some older tenants were deployed with helm-managed SA and never set `create=false`. If we flip TF to manage SA we'll apply a change that may recreate or conflict. we need a migration path.

Tess: migration playbook idea: 
- detect helm-managed SA (check ownerReferences and chart labels)
- mark helm release to `values.serviceAccount.create=false` via a one-off `helm upgrade --reuse-values -f patch.yaml`
- apply TF plan that adds annotation but uses `lifecycle { ignore_changes = ["metadata[0].annotations"] }` during transition? (not ideal)
- preferred: perform a coordinated switchover: patch SA annotation via `kubectl annotate` then import k8s SA resource into TF state with `terraform import kubernetes_service_account.uploader namespace/uploader`

Alex: importing is clean. steps: 1) create the IAM role in TF (no SA annotation yet), 2) annotate the existing SA with the role ARN (`kubectl annotate sa uploader -n <ns> eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn=<arn>`), 3) terraform import the SA resource (use same metadata), 4) run `terraform plan` to ensure no drift, 5) update helm values for chart to `create=false` and set `serviceAccount.name=uploader` so future releases don't touch it.

Samir: do we have an automation checklist for imports?

Morgan: I can write a short script and a runbook. I'll add a preflight check to list tenant namespaces with mismatched annotations:```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
for ns in $(cat tenants.txt); do
  sa=$(kubectl get sa uploader -n $ns -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.eks\.amazonaws\.com/role-arn}' || echo "")
  tf_role=$(terraform state list | grep aws_iam_role | xargs -I{} terraform state show {} 2>/dev/null | grep arn || true)
  if [ -z "$sa" ]; then echo "$ns: no SA annotation"; else echo "$ns: SA-> $sa"; fi
done
```

deploy-bot: deployment triggered by @Morgan: playbook/tenant-sa-reconcile started — job: reconcile-2024-09-11-01

Samir: thanks. I'll start with a single test tenant (staging-tenant-3). can someone review a PR that: 1) adds a `docs/tenant-sa-migration.md` runbook, 2) a small terraform import shim, and 3) helm value patch for staging?

Morgan: ping me on the PR, I'll review and add the preflight script to infra-scripts.

Tess: add a note about RBAC: when we import SA into TF, ownerReferences may affect garbage collection. ensure `kubectl get sa -n <ns> -o yaml` and strip ownerRefs before importing if necessary.

Alex: also ensure prometheus service monitors that reference the SA's labels won't break — check chart hooks.

Samir: will do. tagging here: @Morgan @Tess @Alex — thanks :thumbsup:

Morgan: thanks all. I'll post the initial playbook link in this thread when ready. :eyes:
